status: Definition correspondence only, not B1 availability.
method: UNSD correspondence table and SKOS exact/narrower distinction, as documented in DESIGN.md. No directly applicable public reference alignment found; regressions are not benchmark scores.
scope: Twelve natural-gas/enr FITS leaves; other natural-gas leaves remain pending.

sources.finding: Dry and wet gas are separately defined whole-gas bases; associated/nonassociated are reservoir components. Stored gas is not proved reserves.
Reserve adjustments, revisions, discoveries and ownership transfers differ from year-end reserves and report-year production.
Year-end proved reserves links to RNGR11NUS history titled Expected Future Production; estimated annual production is a separate row.
Referring pages identify this series as dry gas proved reserves as of December 31. The title is not an annual output or forecast measure.
Nonproducing reserves exclude producing reservoirs; they are a subset of proved reserves.
Gas liquids are separated liquid hydrocarbons; they are not whole natural gas or whole petroleum.
EIA publishes crude oil plus lease condensate as its crude reserve total; Table 11 separately reports wet gas reserves and their dry-gas/liquid content.

expectationsBeforeClassifierEdit: Dry Expected Future Production is year-end reserves, distinct from estimated report-year production.
Dry and wet-after-lease-separation total gas reserves and production are whole-gas measurement bases, labelled; no summing them.
Associated, nonassociated, coalbed and shale measures remain subsets of total natural gas.
Nonproducing reserves are subsets even where product names otherwise describe a whole product.
Reserve ownership sales, acquisitions, revisions, extensions and discoveries are outside the locked activities; never gas sales, expenditures or total reserves.
Natural gas liquids and lease condensate are liquid components of petroleum, not whole natural gas. No new qualifier.
Crude oil plus lease condensate remains a subset of petroleum. EIA headline crude basis may qualify only for separately counted explicit crude-oil requests and must be labelled.
Full series names control mixed-product routes; every original definition is retained.
Mapped geography is a separate requirement; districts and federal-offshore components cannot become whole states.
Unknown titles or new process codes remain pending; no catch-all acceptance.
No native definition or compatible combination proves numeric observations or complete history.
